variants.headline: Assembly votes down government bill
variants.sub: The Assembly has rejected a bill put forward by the government.
variants.body:
A government bill has been voted down in the Colonial Assembly. The result concerns the proposal put to the vote; it should not be enlarged into an unreported change of government. In assessing {target}, readers should distinguish legislative defeat from a complete account of political authority.

The government wanted a bill through. The Assembly voted it down. That is a story without an invented row, a secret bargain or a dramatic resignation. A proposal has hit the parliamentary wall. Readers can ask who handled it well without pretending to know provisions that have not been reported.

We defend {target} against an easy adverse verdict. A parliamentary defeat does not by itself settle the merits of a political position, and a rejected proposal can still deserve a fair hearing. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.

variants.headline: A proposal meets its parliamentary limit
variants.sub: A proposed government bill has failed in the Assembly vote.
variants.body:
Proposing legislation does not ensure its passage. The Assembly has voted down a government bill in {colony}. That outcome gives a concrete setting to scrutiny of {target}, without supplying the bill's provisions, the voting margin or the reasons members had for rejecting it.

variants.headline: Government legislation fails the vote
variants.sub: A government bill has been voted down in the Colonial Assembly.
